You are an adversarial deep-tech investor. EXECUTION skeptic: can a tiny team starting with software today actually reach a sellable product? Attack capital needs, hiring, sales cycle, technical risk.
Default to skepticism; score 1-10 where 7+ means you would actually take a meeting. Thesis:
{
  "name": "Helios Fabric (OCS control plane for the non-Google world)",
  "one_liner": "The orchestration and scheduling software that makes reconfigurable optical fabrics actually usable — Google's Apollo topology-engineering stack, productized for everyone buying merchant OCS.",
  "wedge": "Software (topology solver, reconfiguration scheduler, ML-job-aware fabric controller, telemetry) that sits between standard cluster schedulers (Kubernetes, Slurm, SLURM-on-cloud, NVIDIA Base Command) and merchant OCS hardware (Lumentum R300, Coherent, Polatis) via the emerging OCP OCS standard. Initial customer: neoclouds and second-tier AI clouds (CoreWeave-class, sovereign AI datacenters) that want Google-style fabric economics — ~108W optical switch vs ~3000W electrical, <3% of system power — but have zero in-house optical networking software capability. Land with a 'fabric efficiency audit' tool; expand to the control plane.",
  "why_now": "The hardware is arriving before the software: ~20K OCS units ship in 2026 but Google takes ~18K — the other ~2K are landing at operators with no Apollo equivalent. Lumentum is guiding to ~$100M/quarter OCS revenue by end-2026 and needs its boxes to be deployable; Microsoft already runs OCS in 12 Azure zones (18% rack-power reduction reported); OCP launched OCS standardization with Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA and all major vendors in 2025-26, creating the API surface a third-party control plane can target. SemiAnalysis pegs Apollo's value to Google at >$3B — the software is demonstrably where the value is.",
  "market": "Merchant OCS hardware: $0.56B (2026) → ~$2.5B (2029-2032). A control-plane vendor plausibly captures 15-25% of hardware spend as software/subscription (network OS analogy: Arista's EOS economics), so ~$100-500M SAM by 2030 — real but not enormous, and it expands if fast (ns-µs) optical switching for scale-up fabrics materializes (Oriole's PRISM with AMD, 81% core-network power reduction claims), where the same control plane extends to per-collective switching. Honest caveat: Cignal AI explicitly flags OCS-beyond-Google as a possible bubble; this thesis is a call option on a second and third hyperscaler committing.",
  "competition": "Google (has the stack, doesn't sell it — but could open-source pieces and kneecap you); the OCS hardware vendors themselves (Lumentum/Coherent/Polatis will ship basic management software; historically optical vendors are bad at cloud-native control planes, but Lumentum has $100M/quarter of motivation); Oriole Networks/iPronics/Salience (funded, but hardware-led — likely partners before competitors); NVIDIA (the existential one: if optical switching enters its reference architectures, its own fabric manager subsumes you); in-house hyperscaler builds (Microsoft already partially built it).",
  "moat": "Deployment know-how and integration surface: topology solvers tuned on real traffic traces, qualified interop matrix across OCS vendors and ML schedulers, and OCP-standard leadership. Like all infra control planes, the moat is operational trust accumulated in production — thin at first, thick after ten deployments. Realistically this company wins by becoming the default software partner bundled by Lumentum/Coherent, then is acquired by one of them, Cisco, or Arista.",
  "capital_intensity": "Low. Pure software team (6-12) plus a lab with 1-2 OCS units (~$100-300K of hardware — the single meaningful capex item) and GPUs for testbed demos. Seed $4-6M; the constraint is customer access, not capital. Partner with an OCS vendor for lab hardware to cut even that.",
  "software_mvp": "This week: a topology-engineering simulator — ingest an AI cluster spec (GPU count, collective patterns, rail-optimized baseline) and traffic traces, solve for OCS-reconfigurable topologies, and output projected job-completion-time and power savings versus static electrical fabrics, calibrated against published Apollo/Azure numbers. This is a pure-Python artifact that doubles as the sales tool: run it on a prospect's cluster telemetry and show them their number. Follow with an OCP-OCS-standard southbound driver stub.",
  "risks": [
    "The bubble scenario: no operator besides Google/Microsoft deploys OCS at scale and the merchant market stalls at low hundreds of millions — Cignal AI's warning is explicit",
    "Hardware vendors bundle 'good enough' management software free, compressing you to a services company",
    "NVIDIA reference architectures absorb optical switching and its fabric manager becomes the default control plane",
    "Neocloud customers are cash-constrained and slow to adopt operationally exotic networking",
    "Fast-OCS (the expansion story) is still research-grade; the base business alone may not clear venture scale"
  ]
}

## OCP OCS Subproject Launch (July 2025)

In July 2025, the Open Compute Project (OCP) formally launched an OCS sub-project, with founding members including tech giants like Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and Lumentum. The OCS Subproject will facilitate collaboration of open OCS technologies to meet the escalating connectivity demands of high bandwidth, low latency, and energy efficiency in data-intensive applications like artificial intelligence. input.rationale: This is one of the more intellectually honest theses I've seen — the facts check out on verification (Lumentum really is guiding to ~$100M/qtr OCS by end-CY2026 with $400M+ backlog; the OCP OCS subproject really launched July 2025 with Google/Microsoft/NVIDIA/Lumentum/Coherent/Polatis; the April 2026 OCP white paper exists). It is capital-light, the simulator MVP is genuinely buildable by a tiny team this week, and the founder pre-names every kill scenario. But verification also confirms the fatal execution gap: the ~2K non-Google OCS units in 2026 are going to Microsoft, Oracle, Meta, and NVIDIA — hyperscalers who build control planes in-house and will never buy fabric software from a 6-person seed startup — while Cignal AI states non-Google deployments remain at proof-of-concept stage with limited GPU-architecture adoption before 2029. The named wedge customer (neoclouds/CoreWeave-class) does not currently appear in the OCS buyer base at all. So the company is selling a production-critical fabric control plane to a customer segment that has not yet bought the hardware it controls, into one of the hardest trust sales in infrastructure, with a self-admitted $100-500M SAM whose upper bound rests on an unproven 15-25% software attach rate (the Arista/EOS analogy fails — Arista sells the box; standalone network control-plane software at that attach rate has no precedent, cf. the SONiC-ecosystem startups). The thesis's own realistic endgame — become Lumentum's bundled software partner, get acquired by Lumentum/Cisco/Arista — is a sub-$100M outcome that Lumentum could achieve more cheaply by hiring four engineers. Not venture-shaped on execution today; a superb thesis to revisit in 18 months if a second hyperscaler commits and a single neocloud takes OCS delivery. Below the meeting bar, but barely — this founder I would keep warm. Sources: fool.com Q3 FY26 LITE transcript, opencompute.org OCS subproject announcement and April 2026 white paper, cignal.ai Feb 2026 OCS forecast.
fatal_flaws: ICP does not exist yet: verified market data (Cignal AI, Feb 2026) shows the non-Google ~2K units go to Microsoft/Oracle/Meta/NVIDIA — all in-house builders — and non-Google OCS is explicitly 'proof-of-concept and early trial stage' through ~2029. Neoclouds, the named wedge customer, are not buying OCS today; the company would spend its entire seed waiting for its customer segment to materialize.

The sale is a production fabric control plane — the highest-trust purchase in a datacenter. A GPU fabric outage costs a neocloud millions per day; no cash-strapped operator hands reconfiguration authority over their interconnect to a seed-stage vendor with zero production deployments. The moat the thesis correctly identifies ('operational trust after ten deployments') is also the cold-start problem it cannot solve: deployments one through nine have no rational buyer.

Venture-scale math fails even on the thesis's own numbers: $100-500M SAM by 2030, where the upper bound assumes a 15-25% software attach on hardware spend that has no standalone precedent (Arista monetizes EOS through the switch; independent network-control-plane software companies — SONiC startups, Pluribus — compressed to services or sub-scale exits). The thesis's stated realistic outcome, bundle-then-acquisition by Lumentum, is an outcome Lumentum can replicate by hiring the team directly.

NVIDIA subsumption is acknowledged but underweighted: slow (seconds-scale MEMS) OCS reconfiguration is only useful at job-placement granularity — exactly the layer the cluster scheduler and NVIDIA's fabric/mission-control stack already owns for the neocloud segment. If OCS enters NVIDIA reference architectures, the control point this company needs is occupied on day one.
improvements: Replace the neocloud ICP with the only buyers who exist: sovereign AI datacenters and second-tier clouds with a signed OCS purchase order. Gate the raise on 2-3 LOIs from operators who have actually taken Lumentum/Coherent delivery — if none exist, the honest structure is a $1-2M pre-seed to run the simulator-as-audit business as market discovery, not a $4-6M seed.

Make the Lumentum channel the plan, not the fallback: negotiate a formal design-win/bundling agreement (Lumentum has $400M of backlog and a stated need for deployability, and co-leads the OCP subproject with iPronics) before hiring beyond 4 people. Distribution through the hardware vendor is the only way a tiny team ever reaches a production deployment.

De-risk the cold-start trust problem by shipping the control plane in shadow/advisory mode first: read-only telemetry plus recommended reconfigurations that operators apply through their existing tooling, so deployments 1-10 carry zero blast radius.

Prove the simulator against one real customer's traces, not 'published Apollo/Azure numbers' — calibration against Google's marketing figures will not survive technical diligence by any serious infra buyer, and the topology-solver moat is empty without proprietary traffic data.

Hiring plan needs specificity: the required intersection (optical networking + collective-communication-aware scheduling + distributed control planes) is ~a few dozen people worldwide, mostly at Google/Microsoft/NVIDIA on $1M+ packages. Name the two founding engineers or the plan is not credible.
